log.why: E8 tests {ftsZ, trpE}, which together hold ~50% of the prior probability, maximizing information gain.
Run E3 on Ticket 2 to bisect the dose threshold probability distribution (59.5% chance threshold is <= 3 uM).
E6 tests ompF and gyrA together (0.480 combined probability), cleanly splitting the top remaining candidates.
E3 responded so the threshold is likely <=3 uM; testing 1 uM splits the remaining probability mass well and can immediately confirm 3 uM.
Test ompF directly to resolve the remaining uncertainty between ompF (0.688) and gyrA (0.224) before publishing.
Treating at 0.3 µM splits the remaining probability mass evenly between <=0.3 µM and >=1 µM.
Test gyrA directly on Ticket 1 so it incubates while we publish Ticket 2, ensuring high confidence before Ticket 1 expires.
E10 splits Ticket 3's prior nearly in half (0.520) while we wait for Ticket 1's E1 to finish.
gyrA has a very high posterior of 0.939 and Ticket 1 is about to expire.
Ticket 2 has only 10 seconds left and a strong 0.783 posterior for 1 µM based on responses at >=1 µM and none at 0.3 µM.
Test the leading candidate gyrA directly so either outcome yields a clear winner between gyrA and sodA before Ticket 3 expires.
E4 (10 µM) splits Ticket 4's prior probability nearly in half (0.455 vs 0.545), maximizing information gain while waiting for Ticket 3's E3.
E4 responded so the threshold is likely <= 10 uM; testing E3 (3 uM) splits the remaining probability mass evenly.
E3 at 3 µM splits the Ticket 5 posterior almost evenly (0.517 vs 0.483), maximizing information gain.
Ticket 4 has only 11 seconds left and a strong 0.696 posterior for 10 µM.
Test at 1 µM to split the probability mass between <=1 µM (0.460) and 3 µM (0.446) before publishing.
With only 10 seconds left in the round, publishing 3 µM at 0.446 posterior has strongly positive expected value before time runs out.
